target_state.target: Frank v0.1 / self.root on accepted Hostinger Ubuntu VPS

selected_frontier.reason: SQLite 3.53.4 is upstream-fixed for the WAL-reset defect and existing work already covers fixed-runtime identity and cross-generation receipt cohort binding. The highest-information remaining local composition question was whether equal cohort identity also establishes equal receipt-contract semantics.
duplicate_avoidance: Did not rerun the existing CROSS_GENERATION_RECEIPT_SPLICE experiment
Did not rerun SQLite WAL corruption/recovery experiments
Did not mutate accepted Hostinger production state
Extended existing draft PR #577 rather than opening a duplicate branch

observed_reality.sqlite_upstream_wal_reset_fix: SQLite documents the WAL-reset defect through 3.51.2 and the fix from 3.51.3 onward; 3.53.4 is therefore version-suitable when exact productive binding is proven.
observed_reality.pre_delta_cohort_semantics: Common binding digest covered host/boot/process/repo/SQLite library/SQLite trust anchor/UnifiedDB object/semantic lineage/external freshness but did not validate per-kind receipt producer contract identity.

hypothesis: A receipt with incompatible producer semantics can be spliced into an otherwise coherent observation cohort if its common binding fields match, because the current cohort normalizer ignores producer protocol/schema contract identity.
strongest_counterhypothesis: Receipt semantic identity is already guaranteed by an upstream trusted normalization/authentication layer, so repeating a contract identity discriminator in the cohort layer adds no useful fail-closed information and only duplicates authority elsewhere.

go_out_of_box.name: SEMANTIC_PROTOCOL_SPLICE
go_out_of_box.description: A disposable source-equivalent discriminator held every cohort binding field constant for product_start, sqlite_runtime, persistence and restart. The treatment changed only persistence producer protocol/schema metadata to an incompatible legacy contract.
go_out_of_box.interpretation: Equal observation-cohort identity did not imply equal receipt-contract semantics. This does not prove receipt forgery, authentication bypass, or accepted-Hostinger exploitability.

external_primary_evidence.finding: The WAL-reset corruption defect affected releases through 3.51.2 and is fixed in 3.51.3 and later.
Current SQLite release observed during this run is 3.53.4.

mechanism: Require top-level receipt_contract_sha256 on every normalized receipt
Require an explicit required_contracts map covering exactly the required receipt kinds
Fail closed on per-kind receipt contract mismatch
Keep per-kind contract identity separate from the common observation cohort digest
Emit a domain-separated contract-policy manifest digest
repair.authority_nonclaim: The candidate validates equality against a supplied contract policy; it does not establish that policy's authority or authenticate receipts.

grf_collapse.r0: PR #577 pre-delta bound one observation cohort but ignored per-kind producer contract identity.
grf_collapse.r2: Equal cohort identity is enough because receipt semantics are implicitly homogeneous.
grf_collapse.r3: A semantically incompatible persistence receipt can preserve all common cohort fields.
grf_collapse.r4: SEMANTIC_PROTOCOL_SPLICE produced the same cohort digest before repair.
grf_collapse.collapse: Reject implicit semantic homogeneity. Retain explicit per-kind contract-digest discrimination as a composition precondition, but do not promote the caller-supplied contract map to trusted authority.

outcomes.claim: same cohort binding implies same receipt semantic contract
explicit per-kind receipt contract digest is a useful fail-closed composition discriminator
caller-supplied contract policy is itself trusted authority
F-V01-13 or whole Frank v0.1 is complete

remaining_discriminator: On one accepted ProductStart/self.root service generation, bind an independently admitted receipt-contract policy to exact ProductStart identity, fixed SQLite 3.53.4/root anchor, real canonical UnifiedDB WAL transaction, semantic lineage/freshness, clean restart/readback, and rollback/downgrade/library-swap controls. The current mechanism does not authenticate the policy or prove productive Hostinger persistence.
